Econ undergrad & MBA grad degree holder here. I've worked in corporate america, bought a business, and have started multiple businesses from scratch. I'm not going to say that a formal education isn't helpful, because it is....just not how you think it would be. My degrees really didn't teach me anything about starting or running a business. They did prepare me for my journey though. H.S. prepares you for undergrad, undergrad for an entry level job, your 1st job for grad school, grad school for corporate america, corporate america for running your own company.

A 9-5 is daunting for many people, but keep in mind 2 things: First, if you can't hack a 9-5, you will get eaten alive trying to run your own business. Your own business is your life 24-7 when you first start it....that is if you want it to succeed even on a minor level. I'm 3 years into owning my current business and I'm just now coming down to a "light" 55 hours a week on average. When I started, I would say 85 hours a week was average and it consumed all of my waking thought and brainpower. #2 a 9-5 is an absolute great way to learn how to run your own business. I've worked as a globe trotting commodities manager for multi billion dollar companies, but I came up as a car detailer/valet/bartender/sandwich maker/geeksquad member as I worked my way through school. Some of the greatest lessons I've learned along the way where from the most entry level jobs. Honestly, I employ more teachings that I picked up working for Jimmy Johns that I do from my days working as a highly & overpaid "professional" Fortune 500 worker. Good processes and procedures can be found at all types of places.

Franchises are a great places to learn about building your own business. Remember, there is a reason they are so large and so many people are willing to pay them to operate their system....it's because their system works and can be replicated. (Nit, I'm not advocating you buy a franchise here....copy what they do and go at it on your own. franchises make the franchishor rich, not you.).

My advice that I'd give to my sons today: Get a job. Any job will do. Learn everything you can about what makes that business successful. Go to school at night. Take accounting. Take finance. Take econ. Take Rhetoric and learn to talk fast so you can sell. After a few months, get a new job. Learn everything they have to offer. Rinse and repeat until you have your associates or maybe even a bachelors in accounting. Save every penny you can. Read books about start ups. Write down all of your ideas. When you have a great one, start putting it into practice. Set up the company, file paperwork, get a federal tax ID, register with your sec. of state. Do everything you can to have the business set up as a legal entity so you can start selling your idea when its time....because all of this takes a lot of time.

In short, you are going to learn about being a business owner by being a business owner. You draw on your past experience and then you put it into practice. You make mistakes and then you learn from them. With any luck and a lot of perseverance, you'll make it 1 year...then another....then another....and then you'll magically start to make money one day. If you get lucky, you'll survive to tell the tale to some other young people who want to get started in 20 years and maybe you'll have a bit of money in your pocket.

Best of luck.
